speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: asked the Minister for National Development with the conclusion of public consultation on short-term home rentals (a) what are the main feedback and concerns provided by the public during the consultation exercise; (b) when will new regulations be presented to Parliament for debate; (c) how many illegal rentals have there been so far; and (d) how does the Ministry intend to Police the current short-term rental websites before the laws are put in place.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked the Minister for National Development in light of concerns from some condominium owners on the further relaxation on short-term leases (a) whether the Ministry will consider getting 100% approval from current property owners in each condominium before short-term leases like Airbnb can be allowed; (b) whether the potential impact of short-term leases on the hospitality industry has been considered; and (c) how is the Ministry dealing with illegal leasing of property currently listed on websites like Airbnb.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) how many Airbnb cases have been reported in HDB units and private residential units respectively in the past three years; and (b) what is the typical timeframe for investigation to complete after a case has been reported.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Many respondents supported the need for regulations on STA, given that STA can cause negative externalities to other residents.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Key concerns raised include safety, security and privacy, as well as abuse of common property.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Many also supported regulating STA platform operators, for example, through a licensing framework.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One of the proposals was to require the Management Corporation of a strata-titled residential development to obtain the support of at least 80% of the share value in the development before STA can be permitted in any residential unit.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The intent is to give homeowners a say in whether or not to allow STA in their development.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Some respondents felt that an 80% threshold would be unfair to the minority who do not support STA, but have to accept the presence of STA guests in their developments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On the other hand, there were some who felt that an 80% threshold was too high and that it would be difficult to obtain sufficient votes in support of STA among homeowners.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah asked about the impact of legalising STA on the hospitality industry.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Indeed, this is something we had considered very carefully.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The proposed regulatory framework for STA includes controls which are similar to those imposed on the hospitality industry.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, under our proposed safeguards, STA hosts must collect and record the personal details of their guests and comply with fire safety regulations like the provision of fire extinguishers in their units.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have also proposed licensing platform operators, so that they can also help to ensure that STA activities do not cause problems for other residents.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The intent is to provide a more level playing field between the STA sector and the hospitality industry.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As I have mentioned, these are proposals that we had put out; we have done one round of consultation, received feedback, there are mixed views.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, URA is studying the matter very carefully to see what is the best way forward.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: URA will take enforcement action against those who breach this rule.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Alex Yam and Mr Melvin Yong asked about the number of such cases.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The time taken by URA and HDB to investigate a report of unauthorised STA depends on the circumstances of each case.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Conducting ground inspections and interviews to obtain evidence of an offence can take up to several months in some instances.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: However, if the party making the report is able to provide details and documentary evidence of the suspected offence, investigations can be completed more expeditiously.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The impact on the hospitality sector that I am looking at is, with the liberalisation of short-term leases, does the Minister think that it is unfair to those who had invested in the hospitality sector?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They would have invested in the setting up, for example, of hotels and so on.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The second question is, why is it 80%?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Condominium owners, a lot of them who buy and want to stay in these units themselves, they will be adversely affected.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I would think that for existing condominiums, it should be 100%.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The third question, a lot of the residents think that if we allow short-term leases, it would drive up the rental costs and, hence, it would have a chain-effect and drive up the cost of living.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And, last, if we allow short-term leases, it would make investment in a property look more attractive and the returns more attractive and, hence, it would drive up property prices.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: On one hand, you have just implemented a round of cooling measures that is very unpopular; and on the other hand, you wish to liberalise short-term lease.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On the first point on the hospitality sector, our approach to this has to be one that is based on fair competition.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is not possible to say, "Let's block any new entrants into the hospitality sector", simply on the basis that the existing incumbents have put in investments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is an open market; new entrants can come in but the regulations must be fair and the industry must be regulated on a level playing field.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is the intent of what we have proposed.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On the thresholds, as I have said, there were mixed views from the consultations, so, we are going to review what is the right way forward and what is the best way to ensure that all property owners do have a say in deciding on the appropriate use of their development.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On the impact on rental and the property market, the Member's views are well-taken.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have seen this and we have studied this phenomenon in other property markets as well where, indeed, short-term accommodations have put upward pressure on rentals and on property prices.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are mindful that this may have an impact and that is why, as I have said earlier, we are not rushing to make changes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If and when we choose to do so, we will make sure that there are, indeed, appropriate safeguards.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The hon Member Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and I had raised the question on short-term lease websites that are currently operating.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Are there any plans to police them, or to regulate them before the new regulations come into place?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The second, as the Minister has mentioned earlier, the number of cases under URA and HDB, they come close to about 2,200 cases.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Of these reports, how many have actually proceeded to prosecution?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The postings themselves may not necessarily contravene the rules and, even if we were to block the websites, I am sure there will be different ways in which these advertisements can be put up.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, I think the key is not so much the postings or the websites, but the actual STA activities that are undertaken.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And if URA knows of any such activities, they will take follow-up and enforcement action.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There has already been one and we will see if there are others, if they were to come in the subsequent months.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In fact, I think out of the 1,000-over cases, a significant number will be from my constituency.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I just did a quick check on one of the websites: I tried to put in a five-day request and it turns out that there are 196 listings just within a small area in Novena and Orchard.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I think a common complaint from my residents is that URA is taking too long to investigate the complaints and to take enforcement actions to stop the illegal short-term home rentals.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Residents cannot quite understand why it is taking so long because they have pictures of people coming in buses and in Grab cars every two, three days.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In fact, during my house visits, they can even tell me which are the units.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: When I go and knock on the doors, yes, indeed, sometimes, different residents come to talk to me.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, to them, I think the evidence is quite clear and perhaps the investigations and enforcement action can be more expeditious.
